        1.    makes a first claim for REA after reaching pensionable age and

        are in receipt of REA. However, a person who can never be converted to RA can
        continue to receive REA whilst conditions for REA are met.

Check governing headings, definitions, exceptions and current source.","text":"71771   From 24.3.961 a person who reaches (or has already reached) pensionable age is
        regarded as having given up regular employment at the start of the first week
        following

        1.    week commencing 24.3.96 or

        2.    the week in which they reach pensionable age or

        3.    if still in regular employment, the week in which they are no longer in such
              employment
                             2
        whichever is the later . A week is defined as a period of seven days beginning with
        a Sunday3.

        Note: Where employment is seasonal, a person is not in regular employment when
        a seasonal contract ends.

        before 6.4.87 it could go down. If, for example, on renewal, a lower rate was found
        to be appropriate on comparison of earnings, the new award would reflect this. In
        these circumstances

        1.    there was nothing to prevent the rate subsequently increasing again on a
              renewal award but

        2.    the rate could never be greater than that payable on 5.4.87.

        Therefore each claimant affected by this limitation had a personal ceiling on the
        REA rate imposed.
